None of the three solutions is correct. The limit is 1/10.

- **Lower bound:** T₂(Pₙ) is the subgraph of the grid on the staircase region {(i,j) : 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n}, with about n²/2 vertices. Each vertex has maximum degree 4, so a closed neighbourhood has at most 5 vertices, giving γ ≥ (n²/2)/5 = n²/10 asymptotically.
- **Upper bound:** Restrict a perfect dominating set of the infinite grid (density 1/5) to the region. Only the O(n) vertices near the boundary can be left undominated, so γ ≤ n²/10 + O(n).

Solution 1 claims γ = |A| ≈ n²/4, but its lower-bound argument is invalid, and the upper bound above already rules out any value above 1/10. Solutions 2 and 3 give 1/6 and 1/8 with no valid derivation.

CHOICE: NONE
CONFIDENCE: 4
